meta.title: Ondra Onboarding
meta.description: A first-run guide state machine whose four segments are: check the runtime, reuse an installed.ondra. pick a free port, then open the interface with its token. Every segment needs evidence to count as done, because skipping ahead leaves later evidence pointing at nothing; skipping is allowed only on the single optional segment, opening the interface, since some environments have no graphical session at all. The plugin is also the acceptance baseline for the out-of-the-box chapter of the launch video: the installer title is composed from the identity source of truth, the progress percentage is computed rather than hardcoded because the number in the video is one frame and not a constant, the status line uses the two mandated sentences verbatim, and the first message must be initiated by the current persona with its own name in the text - when no name is supplied the plugin reports that instead of signing on the persona's behalf. Each of the five acceptance checks is three-valued: pass, fail, or cannot tell. Treating an unknown as a pass is self-deception, and treating it as a failure is a false alarm. The plugin also absorbs the five high-frequency first-run pitfalls from deployment guides and answers each with the next step rather than a restatement, because four of them share the property that the error does not point at its cause and the fifth reports nothing at all. It renders no interface, sends no message and installs no component: rendering belongs to the interface layer, sending to the dialogue layer, and component installation to the installer.
